title: Customs Duty and Tax Assessment and Enforcement
summary: This thread covers the evolving legal framework for the assessment, imposition, and enforcement of customs duties and taxes, transitioning from the 1969 Act to the Customs Act, 2023. It includes the introduction of modern digital procedures, risk management, and specific duty types like anti-dumping and safeguard duties.

evolution.legal_basis: Shifted from the Customs Act, 1969 to the Customs Act, 2023.
evolution.procedure: Transitioned from manual/paper-based to digital customs computer system declarations.
evolution.enforcement: Introduced risk-based selectivity (yellow lane) and mandatory bank guarantees for transit.

timeline.change: Mandated digital registration (User ID, ESPIN) for customs operations.
Defined 'economic risk' and 'yellow lane' within the context of the Customs Act, 2023.
Established transit/transshipment guarantee requirements and updated definitions for authorized agents.
Implemented specific duty exemptions/reductions for industrial molds and medical equipment, and formalized digital cargo declaration procedures.

Customs Authority: The Customs Authority is responsible for issuing user IDs, passwords, and the Express Service Providers Identification Number (ESPIN) to licensees for performing customs procedures electronically.
The authority must verify that licensees meet the required infrastructure, equipment, and staffing standards before issuing access credentials to the customs computer system.

The authority has the power to suspend or deactivate a licensee's system access credentials and ESPIN without prior notice if the licensee fails to meet operational requirements, commits misconduct, or engages in smuggling and tax evasion.
Express Service Providers Identification: Licensees must obtain an ESPIN from the Customs Authority to process cargo declarations, customs clearance, duty payments, and delivery tracking within the customs computer system.
Automated System: Licensees are required to maintain an automated system capable of connecting to the customs gateway, which must include features for electronic cargo declaration, non-intrusive scanning, real-time tracking, data synchronization, and automated issuance of release notices.

The automated system must support electronic duty payments, automated invoice generation, maintenance of sender and recipient data, and customer-facing portals for shipment tracking and electronic notification of cargo arrival.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: This system serves as the central platform for managing the lifecycle of imported consignments, including declaration, valuation, payment of duties and taxes, and delivery to the customer.

Economic Risk: This is defined as risks related to money laundering, terror financing, proceeds of crime, illegal financial activities, evasion of customs duties and taxes, and trans-national organized economic crime.
Customs Act 2023: Referred to as the Act, this is the primary legislation governing these rules.
Yellow Lane: A selectivity lane in the automated system designated for reviewing documents without requiring physical examination of the goods.
Data Analytics: A method involving the collection, examination, audit, cleansing, and modeling of digital or analog data for the purpose of risk identification and decision-making.
Customs Risk Management Commissionerate: An entity established by the National Board of Revenue for the management of customs risks and implementation of risk management strategies.
Green Channel: A designated passage at entry points for arriving passengers who are not carrying goods subject to customs duties or taxes.
Green Lane: A selectivity lane in the automated system where goods are cleared without document verification, physical examination, or other risk mitigation procedures.
Goods Declaration: Refers to manifests, import or export declarations, and any other information regarding goods or passengers submitted by a person or agent to the customs authority.
Declarant: A person or licensed agent responsible for the clearance of goods, who is liable for the accuracy of all information and documents submitted in a declaration.
Risk: Defined as economic risks and the potential for violation of the Act or any other customs-related laws, rules, or orders during the clearance of goods.
Risk Indicator: Specific criteria used to select and identify high-risk goods consignments or passengers.
Risk Identification: The process of identifying and listing potential risk areas based on information obtained from various sources under risk management protocols.
Risk Assessment: The process of determining the impact, intensity, and likelihood of potential risks through the analysis of identified risk areas.
Risk Management: The lawful activities conducted by the Customs Risk Management Commissionerate to identify, analyze, determine, assess, and control risk areas.
Documents: Defined as any information stored in physical, electronic, or any other medium.
Goods: Defined as per the meaning assigned in Section 2(30) of the Customs Act.
Consignment of Goods: Refers to goods imported, exported, transited, transshipped, or stored in a bonded warehouse, following prescribed methods and forms.
Clearance of Goods: The process of releasing goods from the control of customs authorities upon compliance with all necessary legal and procedural requirements.
Release of Goods: The action taken by customs to hand over goods to the appropriate person or agent after completion of assessment and payment of duties and taxes.
Profile: A collection and analysis system for risk indicators related to importers, exporters, agents, passengers, or goods to determine the appropriate lane (red, yellow, green, blue) or channel for clearance.
Person: Defined as per the meaning assigned in Section 2(39) of the Customs Act.
Blue Lane: A selectivity lane in the automated system where goods are cleared without immediate physical or document verification, pending post-clearance audit.
Manifest Data: Data obtained from vehicle and cargo declarations, Advance Passenger Information (API), Passenger Name Record (PNR), and reports related to inward/outward movement, transit, or transshipment.
Passenger: Defined to include both regular passengers and crew members.
Red Channel: A passage for arriving passengers at entry points who are carrying goods subject to customs duties, restricted goods, or prohibited items.
Red Lane: A selectivity lane in the automated system where selected consignments are subject to document verification and mandatory 100% physical examination.
Selectivity: A function performed by the automated system or manually by the Customs Risk Management Commissionerate to assign specific risk mitigation procedures to a consignment based on risk indicators or random selection.
Automated Risk Management System: An automated system operated by the Customs Risk Management Commissionerate that assesses the likelihood of risk for a consignment or passenger by comparing declaration data against predefined risk indicators.

(২) সংশ্লিষ্ট চুক্তি বা প্রটোকল বা স্ট্যান্ডার্ড অপারেটিং প্রসিডিউর এ উল্লিখিত কাস্টমস বন্ড বা লেটার অব গ্যারান্টি বা অঙ্গীকারনামা সংশ্লিষ্ট ক্ষেত্রে বৈধ গ্যারান্টি হিসেবে বিবেচিত হইবে।
(৩) ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট প্রক্রিয়া সম্পন্ন হওয়ার পরবর্তী ৭ (সাত) কার্য দিবসের মধ্যে ক্ষেত্রমত, কাস্টমস বন্ড বা অঙ্গীকারনামা বা লেটার অব গ্যারান্টির অবমুক্তি নিশ্চিত করিতে হইবে।
(৪) আইনের বিধান অনুসরণপূর্বক একই অনুমোদিত ব্যক্তি বা এজেন্ট কর্তৃক একাধিক ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট কার্যক্রম সম্পাদনের ক্ষেত্রে সমন্বিত গ্যারান্টি দাখিলের সুযোগ প্রদান করা যাইবে।
(৫) সন্তোষজনক কার্যক্রম পরিপালনের রেকর্ড রহিয়াছে এবং পূর্ববর্তী বৎসরে অনূ্যন ২০ (বিশ) টি ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট চালান ব্যবস্থাপনায় অংশগ্রহণ করিয়াছে এইরূপ কোনো অনুমোদিত ব্যক্তি যদি অভ্যন্তরীণ প্রবেশ বন্দর সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস কমিশনারের নিকট আবেদন করেন, তাহা হইলে তাহাকে সমন্বিত গ্যারান্টি প্রদানকারী হিসাবে অনুমোদন প্রদান করা যাইবে।
(৬) কাস্টমস বন্ড বা অঙ্গীকারনামা বা লেটার অব গ্যারান্টি সম্পর্কিত সকল বিধান কাস্টমস ওয়েবসাইট এবং ইন্টারনেটের মাধ্যমে সকলের জন্য সহজলভ্য করিতে হইবে।

Transit and Transshipment: Each transit or transshipment shipment requires an unconditional and continuous bank guarantee from a scheduled bank in Bangladesh for an amount equivalent to the applicable duties and taxes to mitigate revenue risks and prevent irregularities.
Customs bonds, letters of guarantee, or undertakings as specified in relevant agreements, protocols, or standard operating procedures are recognized as valid forms of security.
Customs authorities must ensure the release of bonds or guarantees within a specified number of working days after the completion of the transit or transshipment process.
Authorized agents or persons may submit a consolidated guarantee for multiple transit or transshipment activities in accordance with legal provisions.

Qualified persons who have a record of satisfactory compliance and have managed a minimum threshold of transit or transshipment shipments in the previous year may be approved for consolidated guarantee submission upon application to the customs commissioner.
Customs Authority: The customs authority is responsible for ensuring that all regulations and procedures regarding bonds, letters of guarantee, and undertakings are made easily accessible to the public through the official customs website and the internet.

Authorized Person: An authorized person is defined as a licensed shipping agent, freight forwarder, or clearing and forwarding agent empowered to submit declarations, guarantees, bonds, or letters of undertaking to the customs authorities.
Customs Act 1969: The term Act is defined as the Customs Act 1969 for the purposes of these rules.
Agent: The term agent is defined with reference to the meaning provided in the Customs Act 1969.
Customs Computerised System: The term customs computer system is defined with reference to the meaning provided in the Customs Act 1969.
Customs Transit or Transshipment Declara: This refers to the declaration submitted in a prescribed form via bilateral/multilateral agreements, protocols, SOPs, or National Board of Revenue orders, and includes submissions made within the customs computer system.
Customs Bond or Undertaking or Letter of: This refers to a bank guarantee or undertaking provided on non-judicial stamp paper in a specified manner, covering the equivalent amount of duties and taxes applicable to transit or transshipment goods.
Customs Control: The term customs control is defined with reference to the interpretation provided in the Customs Act 1969.
Customs Station: The term customs station is defined with reference to the meaning provided in the Customs Act 1969.
National Board of Revenue: The term Board is defined as the National Board of Revenue constituted under the National Board of Revenue Order 1972.
Oversized Goods: This refers to machinery or equipment exceeding specific dimensions which are not suitable for containerization.
Conveyance: The term vehicle is defined with reference to the meaning of conveyance provided in the Customs Act 1969.
Customs Duty: The term duty-taxes encompasses various import-level charges including Customs Duty, Regulatory Duty, Countervailing Duty, Anti-Dumping Duty, Safeguard Duty, Value Added Tax, Advance Tax, Supplementary Duty, and Advance Income Tax.
Combined Guarantee: This is a type of guarantee that can be applied to multiple transit or transshipment declarations by the same authorized person, or one that remains active for future operations without needing release after every individual shipment.
Standard Operating Procedure: This refers to the formal procedures established between parties under bilateral or multilateral agreements to facilitate the transit or transshipment of goods.

(২) এই প্রজ্ঞাপনের আওতায় পণ্য আমদানি ও খালাসের লক্ষ্যে প্রতিষ্ঠানটির হালনাগাদ নবায়নকৃত শিল্প ভোক্তা আইআরসি রহিয়াছে এবং ১৩ ডিজিট সংবলিত মূল্য সংযোজন কর (মূসক) নিবন্ধিত প্রতিষ্ঠানটি বিবেচ্য বিল অব এন্ট্রি দাখিলের অব্যবহিত পূর্ববর্তী মাসের মূসক দাখিলপত্র (রিটার্ন) দাখিল করিয়াছে মর্মে কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমে বা ভ্যাট অনলাইন সিস্টেমে বা জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড এর ওয়েবসাইটে বা ভ্যাট কমিশনারেট এর ওয়েবসাইটে ইলেকট্রনিক তথ্য প্রদর্শিত থাকিতে হইবে:

The order necessitates compliance with specific audit requirements as prescribed under this act.
Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: This act provides the enabling power to grant exemptions from value added tax and supplementary duty for specified medical equipment imports.
Hospitals benefiting from these exemptions must comply with the registration, filing, and procedural requirements stipulated in this act.
National Board of Revenue: The board acts as the central authority for issuing these exemptions in the public interest and is responsible for making decisions regarding time extensions for the installation of imported medical equipment.
The board establishes and supervises the committee responsible for physical inspection and verification of the installed equipment.
Industrial IRC Holder: To qualify for duty and tax exemptions, the importing hospital must hold a valid Industrial IRC as an industrial consumer issued by the relevant regulatory authority.
Customs Duty: A specific exemption is provided for customs duty on medical equipment imports, covering the amount exceeding the first one percent of the value-based duty rate.
This exemption applies subject to strict conditions, including mandatory post-import installation and usage verification.
Regulatory Duty: Total exemption is granted from all regulatory duties for the medical equipment listed in the table provided in this order.
Value Added Tax: Total exemption from all value added taxes is granted to qualifying hospitals importing the specified medical equipment, provided all procedural and compliance conditions are met.
Supplementary Duty: Total exemption from all supplementary duties is granted for the medical equipment listed in this order, subject to the fulfillment of prescribed usage and installation conditions.
Advance Tax: Imported medical equipment listed in the table is exempted from all advance tax payments, provided the importing hospital maintains compliance with all regulatory conditions.
Hospital: The term refers to multi-disciplinary or mono-disciplinary medical facilities that meet specific criteria, including a minimum bed capacity and free service provisions for the poor.
Hospitals must adhere to strict installation deadlines for imported equipment and are subject to mandatory system-based audits every three years to retain their concessionary status.
Indemnity Bond: Importing hospitals must execute and submit an indemnity bond on non-judicial stamp paper to the customs authority, covering the amount of exempted duties and taxes, which remains subject to return upon successful verification of equipment installation.
System Based Audit: Hospitals utilizing these concessionary benefits are mandatorily required to undergo a system-based audit every three years to ensure continued compliance with customs regulations.

Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: For shipments where cargo declaration cannot be filed electronically as a single entry, the system allows for the submission of declarations based on transport documents like bills of lading, airway bills, or transport receipts.
The system may be used to uniquely flag shipments using specific import codes and is responsible for providing exit numbers and ensuring port release after data verification.
Except for shipments selected for physical inspection under risk management, the system facilitates the verification of declarations and the payment of duties and taxes for clearance.
Import Clearance: Clearance is granted for shipments based on transport documents when standard electronic cargo declaration is not feasible, provided the goods are not selected for physical examination under risk management.
Risk Management: Shipments are subjected to risk assessment, where physical examination remains mandatory for those selected by the system, while others may proceed based on the authenticity of the submitted declarations.

118B. Imposition of anti-dumping duty.- (1) Where any goods are exported from any country or territory (hereinafter in this section referred to as the exporting country or territory) to Bangladesh at less than the normal value, then, upon the importation of such goods into Bangladesh, the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, impose an anti-dumping duty not exceeding the margin of dumping in relation to such goods.
Explanation.- For the purposes of this section,-
(a) "margin of dumping", in relation to any goods, means the difference between its export price and its normal value;
(b) "export price", in relation to any goods, means the price of the goods exported from the exporting country or territory and in cases where there is no export price or where the export price is unreliable because of association or a compensatory arrangement between the exporter and the importer of a third party, the export price may be constructed on the basis of the price at which the imported goods are first resold to an independent buyer, or not resold in the condition as imported, on such reasonable basis as may be determined in accordance with the rules made under sub-section (6);
(c) "normal value", in relation to any goods, means-
(i) the comparable price, in the ordinary course of trade, for the like goods when meant for consumption in the exporting country or territory as determined in accordance with the rules made under sub-section (6); or
(ii) when there are no sales of the like goods in the ordinary course of trade in the domestic market of the exporting country or territory, or, when because of the particular market situation or low volume of the sales in the domestic market of the exporting country or territory, such sales do not permit a proper comparison the normal value shall be either-
(a) comparable representative price of the like goods when exported from the exporting country or territory or an appropriate third country as determined in accordance with the rules made under sub-section (6); or
(b) the cost of production of the said goods in the country of origin along with reasonable addition for administrative, selling and general costs and for profits, as determined in accordance with the rules made under sub-section (6):
Provided that in the case of import of the goods from a country other than the country of origin and where the goods have been merely transhipped through the country of export or such goods are not produced in the country of export, the normal value shall be determined with reference to the price in country of origin.
(2) The Government may, pending the determination of the normal value and the margin of dumping in relation to any goods, in accordance with the provisions of this section and the rules made thereunder, impose on the importation of such goods into Bangladesh an anti-dumping duty on the basis of a provisional estimate of such value and margin and if such anti-dumping duty exceeds the margin as so determined-
(a) the Government shall, having regard to such determination and as soon as may be after such determination, reduce such anti- dumping duty; and
(b) refund shall be made of so much of the anti-dumping duty which has been collected as is in excess of anti-dumping duty as so reduced.
(3) If the Government, in respect of the dumped goods under inquiry, is of the opinion that-
(i) there is a history of dumping which caused injury or that the importer was, or should have been, aware that the exporter practices dumping and that such dumping cause injury; and
(ii) the injury is caused by massive dumping of goods imported in a relative short time which in light of the timing and the volume of imported goods dumped and other circumstances, is likely to seriously undermine the remedial effect of the anti-dumping duty liable to be levied, the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, levy anti-dumping duty retrospectively from a date prior to the date of imposition of anti-dumping duty under sub-section (2) but not beyond ninety days from the date of notification under that sub-section and notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, such duty shall be payable at such rate and from such date as may be specified in the notification.
(4) The anti-dumping duty chargeable under this section shall be in addition to any other duty imposed under this Act or any other law for the time being in force.
(5) The anti-dumping duty imposed under this section shall, unless revoked earlier, cease to have effect on the expiry of five years from the date of such imposition:
Provided that if the Government, in a view, is of the opinion that the cessation of such duty is likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury, it may, from time to time, extend the period of such imposition for a further period of five years and such further period shall commence from the date of order of such extension:
Provided further that where a review initiated before the expiry of the aforesaid period of five years has not come to a conclusion before such expiry, the anti-dumping duty may continue to remain in force pending outcome of such a review for a further period not exceeding one year.
(6) The margin of dumping as referred to in sub-section (1) or sub- section (2) shall, from time to time, be ascertained and determined by the Government after such inquiry as it may consider necessary and the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, make rules for the purposes of this section and without prejudice to the generality of the forgoing, such rules may provide for the manner in which goods liable for anti-dumping duty under this section may be identified and for the manner in which the export price and the normal value of and the margin of dumping in relation to such goods may be determined and for the assessment and collection of such anti-dumping duty.
(7) No proceeding for imposition of anti-dumping duty under this section shall commence unless the Bangladesh Tariff Commission, on receipt of written application by or on behalf of a domestic industry, informs the Government that there is prima-facie evidence of injury which is caused by dumping on any particular imported goods.]

Anti-Dumping Duty: The Government is empowered to impose an anti-dumping duty on goods imported into Bangladesh at prices below their normal value, provided the duty does not exceed the calculated dumping margin.
Anti-dumping duty acts as a supplementary levy in addition to any other duties or taxes applicable under existing laws and is typically subject to a five-year term unless extended or revoked.

The Government may levy anti-dumping duties retrospectively in cases where massive dumping occurs within a short period and causes injury, subject to specific time limits and evidentiary requirements.
Dumping Margin: The margin of dumping is defined as the difference between the normal value of goods and their export price, serving as the ceiling for the anti-dumping duty that can be imposed.
The Government is responsible for ascertaining and determining the margin of dumping through necessary inquiries and may establish rules to regulate this determination process.
Export Price: Export price represents the price of goods exported from a country to Bangladesh, which may be constructed based on resale prices to independent buyers when direct price information is unreliable due to arrangements between the exporter and importer.
Normal Value: Normal value refers to the comparable price of like goods sold for consumption in the exporting country, or alternatively, the cost of production in the country of origin plus reasonable costs and profits if domestic market data is unavailable.

In instances where goods are transhipped through a third country rather than being exported directly from the country of origin, the normal value is determined with reference to prices in the country of origin.
Government: The Government has the authority to issue official notifications for the imposition, extension, or retrospective application of anti-dumping duties and to frame rules for the assessment and collection of such levies.
Provisional Assessment of Customs Duty: Pending final determination of the normal value and dumping margin, the Government may impose a provisional anti-dumping duty, which is subject to adjustment and refund if it exceeds the finally determined margin.
Bangladesh Tariff Commission: The Bangladesh Tariff Commission serves as the gateway for initiating anti-dumping proceedings by verifying and reporting to the Government whether there is prima-facie evidence of injury caused to local industry by dumping.
Local Industry: Domestic industry may initiate anti-dumping investigations by submitting a written application to the Bangladesh Tariff Commission to demonstrate that imported goods are causing injury due to dumping practices.
Rules: The Government may make rules to prescribe the procedures for identifying dumped goods, calculating export prices and normal values, determining dumping margins, and managing the assessment and collection of anti-dumping duties.

Civil Court: The jurisdiction of civil courts is barred in matters concerning the determination of the legality or propriety of orders or decisions related to customs duties and taxes.

Customs Duty: The Act prohibits civil litigation regarding the levy, imposition, exemption, assessment, or realization of customs duties and taxes.
Officer of Customs: Orders or decisions made by an officer of customs regarding the assessment or collection of duties and taxes are excluded from the jurisdiction of civil courts.
National Board of Revenue: Decisions made by the Board concerning the assessment or collection of customs duties are shielded from review by civil courts.
Government: Orders and decisions issued by the Government regarding customs duties and taxes are not subject to challenge in civil courts.

member_objects.clause_title: Power to refuse port-clearance to vessels or permission for departure to other conveyance

Port Clearance: The appropriate officer of customs has the authority to refuse port clearance to a vessel or permission for departure to other conveyances until all relevant legal requirements and payments are satisfied.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is empowered to demand security, guarantees, or deposits to ensure the payment of dues, taxes, and penalties before granting departure permission to a conveyance.
The officer may require the unloading of goods exported in violation of the law or, if unloading is impractical, demand an undertaking and security for bringing the goods back to Bangladesh.
Conveyance: Departure permission for any conveyance may be withheld until all port dues, charges, and penalties applicable to the conveyance or its person-in-charge have been settled.
Vessel: Port clearance for a vessel may be withheld until all applicable port dues, penalties, and taxes related to the vessel, its master, or its cargo have been paid or secured.
Agent: An agent may provide a written declaration assuming liability for specific penalties and furnish security, thereby becoming responsible for such discharge.
An agent may provide a written declaration assuming responsibility for claims regarding damage or short delivery of imported goods, becoming legally bound to discharge those claims.
Person in Charge: The person-in-charge of a conveyance is responsible for the payment of all dues, taxes, and penalties related to the conveyance or its cargo before departure is permitted.
Export Goods: If export goods are loaded without paying required taxes or duties, or in violation of law, they must be unloaded or the agent must provide an undertaking and security to bring the goods back to Bangladesh.
